title: Synthesize release brief and cross-functional redline tracker
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a single synthesized release brief that serves both internal stakeholders (engineering, SRE, Docs, CS, Sales) and a trimmed, customer-facing changelog. Pair the brief with a cross-functional redline tracker that records reviewer comments, required edits, and final signoffs. Deliverables: 1) Internal release brief (one-pager + FAQ), 2) Customer-ready changelog snippet and migration guidance, 3) Redline tracker (sheet) with owner, SLA, and blocking items, 4) Publishing checklist that ties to console release and SDK bumps.
acceptance_criteria: Internal brief circulated and approved by Eng, Docs, Legal, and Security
Customer-facing changelog copy signed off by PM and Legal and staged in docs repo
Redline tracker has no open blocker tags older than 48 hours before release
Publishing checklist validated in staging and linked to release PR
rollout_plan_summary: Staged rollout by customer tier: 5% beta -> 25% next window -> 100% after 72h monitoring. Console feature flag will gate changes. SDK patch release scheduled same day with migration notes.
internal_summary: Runtime 1.22 introduces batching kernel improvements and a prefix cache optimization expected to reduce median token latency by ~12% on p4d. Internal brief includes SLO impact, rollback playbook, ops runbook link, and cost delta estimates per model class.
customer_facing_snippet: We’ve improved serving performance and reduced latency for commonly used generation flows. No action required for most customers; if you pin a specific runtime, follow the migration guide for SDK changes.
decisions: Publish single-tier customer changelog (no per-model callouts) to reduce noise
Redline owner model: PM owns content, Eng owns performance claims, Legal owns compliance wording
24-hour review SLA for non-blocking edits; 48-hour SLA for legal redactions
tradeoffs: Speed of publication vs. thorough legal redaction: will delay release notes by up to 48h for regulated regions
Granularity of customer-facing text vs. support volume: more technical detail reduces confusion for platform teams but risks higher support churn from general customers

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Late legal redaction causing release freeze. Mitigation: Pre-approved safe phrasing templates for EU/regulated customers.
Risk: Performance regression for edge models. Mitigation: Canary 5% and automatic rollback policy tied to SLO breach metrics.
Risk: Customer confusion about pinned runtimes. Mitigation: Clear migration examples and banners in Console for customers on pinned versions.
